title: Maximum Number That Makes Result of Bitwise AND Zero
summary: For an integer n, find the largest integer x where x is less than or equal to n, and the bitwise AND of all numbers from x to n equals zero.
statement: For an integer n, find the largest integer x where x is less than or equal to n, and the bitwise AND of all numbers from x to n equals zero.
constraints: The bitwise AND of every integer from x through n inclusive must be zero.
hints: Let 2^b be the highest power of two no greater than n.
The number 2^b-1 is immediately below that boundary and shares no high bit with n.
Any larger x retains the high bit across the whole interval until n.
Thus the all-ones value below the top bit is the largest feasible start.
editorial: Thus the all-ones value below the top bit is the largest feasible start.

tests.explanation: Starting at three gives 3&4&5&6&7=0, while any larger start keeps a set bit.
Seven and eight already AND to zero, so seven is maximal.
